description: Write and deliver a 4-6 minute speech introducing yourself to the club on any topic (humorous, informational, or any style). The first project in every path; teaches the basic structure of a public speech and gets you speaking before an audience.

Pick a topic narrow enough for a 5-7 minute speech, clearly define your purpose and goal, organize the speech well, then present it at a club meeting. Level 1 core project teaching basic speech-writing and organization.

exercise_name: Introduction to Vocal Variety and Body Language
description: Deliver a 5-7 minute speech on any topic where the evaluation focuses specifically on either your vocal variety or your body language and gestures; you name the skills you are working on before you speak. Level 1 core project.

Give a 5-7 minute speech on any topic, review the feedback you receive, then give a second 5-7 minute speech (same or new) that incorporates that feedback; you also serve as an evaluator for another member's speech. Level 1 core project on giving and applying feedback.

Complete the Discover Your Leadership Style questionnaire, then deliver a 5-7 minute speech about your leadership style and how it impacts the people around you. Dynamic Leadership Level 2 core project.

Complete the Discover Your Communication Style questionnaire, then deliver a 5-7 minute speech about your communication style and its impact on your professional and personal relationships. Level 2 core project across several paths.
Write and present a 5-7 minute speech about a time when you were a protege and the impact of having a mentor. Required for every member in every path; defines how Toastmasters envisions mentoring.

Develop and deliver a 5-7 minute speech on a topic unfamiliar to most of your club audience, monitoring their reaction and adapting in real time to maintain engagement. Level 2 core / shared elective for connecting with an unfamiliar audience.

Give a 5-7 minute speech on a topic of your choosing that includes at least one anecdote or story intended to entertain or bring humor; the start of building a personal collection of humorous stories. Engaging Humor Level 2 core project.

Develop a 5-7 minute speech on any topic while recording the time you spend on each task, to observe and improve your own time-management patterns, then present it. Leadership Development Level 2 core project.

Keep a journal of your emotions and their impact on you and others for at least two weeks, then discuss the experience in a 5-7 minute speech. Motivational Strategies Level 2 core project on cultivating self- and other-awareness.

Complete a conflict-resolution video activity, then give a 5-7 minute speech on how you manage conflict, how to build a stronger strategy, and your best attributes in conflict situations. Strategic Relationships path core project.
Develop and deliver a 5-7 minute speech about a past or upcoming negotiation in your life, reflecting on the negotiation strategies you used or would use. Dynamic Leadership Level 3 core project.

Give a 5-7 minute speech on your point of view and what makes things funny to you, including at least one anecdote or story, applying your personal style of humor to a central message. Engaging Humor Level 3 core project.

Lead a group of people toward consensus on a challenging topic at a club meeting within 20 minutes, then give a 2-3 minute closing statement on the experience. Effective Coaching Level 3 core project.

Develop a proposal to improve some area of your personal, professional, or Toastmasters life and present it (or an aspect of it) in a 5-7 minute speech at a club meeting. Innovative Planning Level 3 core project.

Choose a small-scale project (party, trip, themed meeting), develop and implement a plan, then deliver a 2-3 minute report or 5-7 minute speech about the experience. Leadership Development Level 3 core project.

Choose any topic that lends itself to persuasion, prepare and deliver a 5-7 minute persuasive speech at a club meeting, after learning the different types of persuasive speech. Persuasive Influence Level 3 core project.

Build a communication plan formulating a central message for a target audience (real or hypothetical event), then present a 5-7 minute speech about the planning process and its benefits or impact. Visionary Communication Level 3 core project.

Work with a small team to collaborate and make decisions on a small-scale project (such as planning a club meeting), then deliver a 5-7 minute speech about your experience with the collaboration process. Team Collaboration path core project.

Create a change-management plan for a real or hypothetical situation in your personal, Toastmasters, or professional life, then share the plan in a 5-7 minute speech. Dynamic Leadership Level 4 core project.

exercise_name: The Power of Humor in an Impromptu Speech
description: Deliver two 2-3 minute impromptu speeches on random topics drawn by the Toastmaster of the Day, each weaving in at least one rehearsed anecdote related to the topic. Engaging Humor Level 4 core project blending quick-wit and humor.

Coach an individual (a club member or someone outside Toastmasters) through a project outside club meetings, then present a 5-7 minute speech about your coaching experience. Effective Coaching Level 4 core project.

Form a team of 3-4 people, create and present a project plan in a 2-3 minute speech, complete the project with your team, then deliver a 5-7 minute speech on the experience. Innovative Planning Level 4 core project.
Build a team of 2-4 people, lead them to complete a project of your design, then present a 5-7 minute speech about your experience leading the team. Leadership Development Level 4 core project.

Build a team of 3-4 people to create and complete a project benefiting your club, applying tailored motivational strategies to each member, then deliver a 5-7 minute speech about the experience. Motivational Strategies Level 4 core project.

Design a project plan, share it in a 5-7 minute speech, then have club members propose disruptions and respond on the spot with strategies for adjusting to unexpected changes. Persuasive Influence Level 4 core project.
Develop a plan for communicating a change to an affected audience, then communicate that real or hypothetical change in a 5-7 minute speech. Visionary Communication Level 4 core project.

Serve in a leadership role (in Toastmasters, another volunteer org, or your career) for at least six months, gather a 360-degree evaluation from peers, and present an 8-10 minute speech about your leadership experience. Dynamic Leadership Level 5 capstone.

Select a project, form a guidance committee that meets at least five times, lead a team of 3+ to complete it, and deliver two 5-7 minute speeches (introducing the plan, then sharing the outcome). Level 5 capstone for several paths.
Write and present an 18-22 minute keynote-style humorous speech (optionally with visual aids), the longest humor project in the program. Engaging Humor Level 5 capstone.
Plan, coordinate, lead, and complete an event of your choosing, then present a 5-7 minute speech sharing the impact of the planning process and your team. Leadership Development Level 5 capstone.

Build and work with a small team to design and host a team-building event; deliver a 2-3 minute report on your plans beforehand and a 5-7 minute speech after the event. Motivational Strategies Level 5 capstone.

Develop a detailed vision for your personal life, professional life, or an organization; present it in a 5-7 minute speech, then later deliver a second 5-7 minute speech presenting your plan to bring the vision to fruition. Visionary Communication Level 5 capstone.
Present a 10-12 minute speech reflecting on your growth across an entire path, summarizing the skills you developed and celebrating your achievements. Required Level 5 closing project in every path.

Choose an established story, a personal story, or a fictional tale of your own creation and deliver a 5-7 minute speech that uses a story (or is a story) to connect with the audience. Popular Level 3 elective on storytelling and descriptive skills.

Practice the difference between literal and figurative language and write a 5-7 minute speech that describes a topic in vivid detail to increase interest and impact, then present it. Level 3 elective.
Develop two different 3-4 minute social speeches (toast, eulogy, acceptance speech, or speech praising an individual/group) and present them at two separate club meetings. Level 3 elective.
Select a topic with the intent of inspiring others and prepare and deliver a 5-7 minute inspirational speech for your club. Level 3 elective on inspirational speaking.

Keep a daily record of your moods, successes, and gratitude for at least two weeks, evaluate the changes, then share an aspect of the experience in a 2-3 minute report or 5-7 minute speech. Level 3 elective on awareness and positivity.

Prepare for and attend a networking event, then present a 5-7 minute speech to your club with stories or lessons from the experience or the benefits of networking. Level 3 elective on building connections.
Choose a type of interview to practice (e.g. job or expert), prepare your skills and abilities, then do a 5-7 minute role-play interview with a club member acting as interviewer. Level 3 elective.

Use the project's exercises to improve your vocal variety, then present a 5-7 minute speech on any topic where the evaluation focuses specifically on your use of volume, pitch, rate, and quality. Level 3 elective.

Prepare a 5-7 minute speech on a topic suited to movement and gestures, video-record it (or rehearse before a mirror) and get feedback, then deliver it with deliberate awareness of intentional and unintentional body language. Level 3 elective.

Fulfill the role of Topicsmaster at a club meeting and comment on each speaker's Table Topics response to demonstrate your active listening, summarizing back what each speaker conveyed. Level 3 elective rooted in the meeting role.
Choose an unfamiliar topic narrow enough for a 5-7 minute speech, research it, organize the information, and present a well-researched, well-organized speech. Level 3 elective on research methods.
Select a topic suited to a visual presentation, develop slides, and give a 5-7 minute speech supported by the slides you created. Level 3 elective on presentation software / slides.
Choose a topic that lends itself to visual aids, create one to three visual aids, and deliver a 5-7 minute presentation using them. Level 3 elective on selecting and using visual aids.
Develop a 5-7 minute speech about the cultures you most closely identify with and the personal impact of the stereotypes associated with them. Level 3 elective on cultural identity and stereotypes.
Complete self-evaluation resources about your goals and readiness to mentor, then discuss being a Toastmasters mentor with your VP Education. Level 3 elective (preparation, no speech).

Work with a protege (matched by your VP Education) to complete a single project, setting goals and giving/receiving feedback, then deliver a speech about the experience. Level 3 elective on short-term mentoring.
Record at least 60 minutes of original podcast content (episodes of 10+ minutes each), then play a 5-10 minute segment in your club introduced by a 2-3 minute speech. Level 4 elective on podcasting.

Build a new social media presence or enhance an existing one toward a personal or professional goal, then deliver a 5-7 minute speech about your results and the benefits of social media. Level 4 elective.
Post at least eight blog entries in one month, then deliver a 2-3 minute speech about the impact of the blogging experience. Level 4 elective on blogging.

Conduct a 20-25 minute online meeting or webinar (with visual aids) for fellow Toastmasters, choosing your topic and software, with your evaluator participating. Level 4 elective on facilitating online meetings.
Choose a topic you know well, deliver a speech on it, then field a question-and-answer session; the speech plus Q&A together must run 15-20 minutes. Level 4 elective on handling impromptu questions.

Prepare a 5-7 minute speech and present it while club members role-play disruptive audience behaviors; you are evaluated on how calmly and professionally you handle the disruptions rather than on the speech content. Level 4 elective.
Create a public relations plan for a real or hypothetical group or situation, then share the plan and how you would apply it in a 5-7 minute speech. Level 4 elective.
Plan and moderate a 20-40 minute panel discussion on any topic, applying public-speaking and leadership skills to facilitate panelists and audience questions. Level 5 elective.
Define your own ethical framework, then organize and moderate a 20-40 minute panel discussion about ethics followed by a Q&A session. Level 5 elective.
Serve in a leadership role in a volunteer organization for at least six months, gather a 360-degree evaluation, create a succession plan, then speak about the experience. Level 5 elective.

Write and present an 18-22 minute keynote-style speech exemplifying the point of view or message you would convey as a professional-level speaker (optionally with visual aids). Level 5 elective, the program's longest non-humor speech.

Facilitate a lessons-learned meeting for a team you have worked with, organize and lead the discussion, and record the results into a reusable document. Level 5 elective on facilitation and reflection.

Serve as a mentor for a fellow Toastmaster or other person for six months, communicating regularly and exchanging written and verbal feedback, then present a 5-7 minute speech about what you gained. Level 5 elective on long-term mentoring.

Design and complete a multifaceted team project benefiting an organization: present a 5-7 minute plan speech, lead the team, gather a 360-degree evaluation, then give an 8-10 minute speech reviewing outcomes and lessons. Capstone for the DTM award after completing two paths.

Classic Competent Communication manual project 1: deliver a 4-6 minute speech introducing yourself to the club, to begin speaking before an audience and identify existing and developing speaking skills.
Classic CC manual project 2 (5-7 min): select an appropriate outline so listeners can easily follow your speech, and build strong opening and closing sections with clear transitions.

exercise_name: CC3 - Get to the Point (classic manual)
description: Classic CC manual project 3 (5-7 min): determine your speech's general and specific purposes, organize the speech to achieve them, and deliver it without notes while projecting sincerity and conviction.

exercise_name: CC4 - How to Say It (classic manual)
description: Classic CC manual project 4 (5-7 min): choose precise, descriptive language and rhetorical/literary devices to communicate ideas clearly, while eliminating jargon and unnecessary words.
Classic CC manual project 5 (5-7 min): use stance, movement, gestures, facial expressions, and eye contact naturally and purposefully to reinforce your message.
Classic CC manual project 6 (5-7 min): use volume, pitch, rate, and quality of voice plus strategic pauses to add interest and meaning and reflect the emotion behind your message.
Classic CC manual project 7 (5-7 min): collect information about your topic from numerous sources and support your points with researched facts, examples, and illustrations.

exercise_name: CC8 - Get Comfortable with Visual Aids (classic manual)
description: Classic CC manual project 8 (5-7 min): select appropriate visual aids for your topic and audience and use them smoothly, correctly, and confidently during the speech.
Classic CC manual project 9 (5-7 min): persuade listeners to adopt your viewpoint or take action using logic, emotion, and appeals to the audience's interests, without notes.

Classic CC manual project 10 (8-10 min): inspire the audience by appealing to noble motives and higher aspirations using stories and anecdotes, delivered without notes. The capstone of the Competent Communication manual.

The recurring impromptu-speaking segment of every meeting: the Topicsmaster poses a surprise prompt and you deliver a 1-2 minute unprepared speech on the spot, with no preparation. The canonical Toastmasters quick-wit / impromptu drill.

Recurring meeting role: prepare a set of impromptu prompts, run the Table Topics segment, call on members to speak off the cuff, and manage the segment's flow and timing. The role behind the Active Listening project.

Recurring meeting role: introduce a Word of the Day, listen for its use and for the quality of English/grammar throughout the meeting, then give a 1-minute report on the best and worst uses of language and how often the word was used. Trains attentive listening and vocabulary.

Recurring meeting role: count and note filler words and sounds (um, ah, er, and, so, you know) used by every speaker during the meeting, then report the tallies. Trains awareness of disfluencies in others and yourself.

Recurring meeting role: monitor the time for each meeting segment and each speaker, signal speakers with green/yellow/red cues, and report each participant's name and elapsed time. Builds awareness of pacing and time discipline.

Recurring meeting role: observe a member's prepared speech against its objectives and deliver a 2-3 minute constructive verbal evaluation highlighting strengths and specific areas to improve. The core feedback skill of the format.

Recurring meeting role: evaluate everything that happens during the meeting and manage the evaluation team (speech evaluators, grammarian, ah-counter, timer), introducing each and then delivering an overall evaluation of the meeting. Builds higher-level observation and feedback skills.

Recurring meeting role: act as the meeting's director and host, getting the agenda, ensuring everyone knows their role, introducing speakers with their topic/objectives/time, and ensuring smooth transitions. Builds facilitation, organization, and on-the-fly hosting skills.
